STRICT THREE-CHARACTER REPLACEMENT: VIDEO EDITING

Replace ONLY the three target characters in the original video [Video 1]:
- Replace the driver (front seat, on the RIGHT of the frame, both hands on the steering wheel, in round dark sunglasses, a black cap and a light-blue patterned jacket) with [Image 2].
- Replace the front passenger (front seat, on the LEFT of the frame, who leads the song, in a black beanie and a blue, red, yellow and white track jacket) with [Image 1].
- Replace the rear-seat left character (behind the front passenger, in a yellow cap and a blue shirt with yellow roses) with [Image 3].
- Do NOT replace the rear-seat right character (behind the driver): the bearded man with glasses in the red plaid shirt stays exactly as in the video.

Use [Image 1], [Image 2], and [Image 3] strictly as the ONLY identity references for the replacement characters. For each one, preserve that image's exact face, facial identity, hairstyle, hair color, skin tone, gender, body proportions, clothing appearance, and recognizable features. Do NOT blend any image with the original character in that seat.

Each replacement character must inherit the original character's (in the same seat): exact position and body placement, exact scale and proportions in frame, exact pose and posture, exact head direction and eye direction, exact mouth movement and lip-sync, exact facial expressions, exact hand and body movements, exact speaking performance, exact movement timing and trajectory, exact interaction with the car interior and other characters.

The replacement characters must follow the original characters' movements naturally and accurately throughout the ENTIRE video.

Preserve the original mouth shapes, speech timing, lip-sync, facial performance, and pose of each character. Do NOT change the speaking rhythm, mouth opening patterns, or dialogue timing.

Preserve EVERYTHING ELSE from the original video exactly: camera movement, zoom and camera motion, framing and composition, lighting and shadows, background, car interior, environment outside the car, timing and duration, objects and props, scene transitions, depth of field, motion blur.

Do NOT alter the background. Do NOT alter the car interior. Do NOT alter the camera. Do NOT alter the composition. Do NOT change the characters' original poses or actions. Do NOT create additional people. Do NOT change the number of people in the scene.

IMPORTANT: ONLY replace the driver with [Image 2], the front passenger with [Image 1] and the rear-seat left character with [Image 3].

Keep the original lip-sync, mouth movement, posture, and performance unchanged. Everything else must remain identical to the original video.

In EVERY shot, also when small in the wide shots, copy each new face exactly from its own photo: face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles. Each new person wears the clothes from their own photo. NO black beanie and NO track jacket on [Image 1], NO round dark sunglasses and NO black cap on [Image 2], NO yellow cap on [Image 3], unless their own photo shows them.

The same three real people in every frame, so their friends instantly recognize them. Never morph, never drift back to the original faces, never add or remove facial hair. Do not mix the faces: each photo is one seat only, and no photo face goes onto the bearded man in the plaid shirt.

Shots, matching the reference: 0-1.2 s the whole cabin from the dashboard, the front passenger ([Image 1]) on the left, the driver ([Image 2]) on the right; 1.2-2.4 s the back seat: [Image 3] on the left, the bearded man in the plaid shirt on the right; 2.4-3.9 s the whole cabin; 3.9-6.1 s close-up of [Image 1] rapping to the camera; 6.1-7.2 s the back seat from the side; 7.2-8.3 s close-up of [Image 1]; 8.3-9.6 s the whole cabin; 9.6-10.6 s the back seat; 10.6-12.8 s close-up of [Image 1]; 12.8-13.7 s the back seat; 13.7 s to the end close-up of [Image 1].

Anatomy rules: one head per person, on that person's own shoulders. A face never appears on hands, clothes, seats or headrests. Exactly four people. No text, no logos.
